forum.title: How to open files on Host PC with fopen on STM32L5
forum.best_answer_content:
You never said that's what you're trying to achieve in *this* thread!

In that case, you will need to have something on the PC which sends the data to the Target.

The PC *pushes* to the Target - the Target doesn't *pull* from the PC.

CubeProgrammer can do this, and is ideal for use with the STM32 System Bootloader:

[**AN2606**](https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/an2606-stm32-microcontroller-system-memory-boot-mode-stmicroelectronics.pdf): *Introduction to system memory boot mode on STM32 MCUs*

**[AN3155](https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/an3155-how-to-use-usart-protocol-in-bootloader-on-stm32-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf):***How to use USART protocol in bootloader on STM32 MCUs*

If you're making a custom bootloader, then you'll have to define your own protocol; eg,

[**AN4657**](https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/an4657-stm32-inapplication-programming-iap-using-the-usart-stmicroelectronics.pdf): *STM32 in-application programming (IAP) using the USART* - uses the YMODEM protocol, which is widely supported by terminal emulators & serial comms libraries/frameworks.

There's also [ST Open Bootloader](http://ST%20Open Bootloader) - also works with CubeProgrammer

Opening a file on the host or doing other host-related system calls is called semi-hosting and need special steps:
How to use semihosting with STM32CubeIDE and STM32 - STMicroelectronics Community

The downside is, that this requires a driver on the host and is said to be slow.
